hints: Shortest distance is the primary criterion; among shortest routes, count paths and track minimum and maximum edge counts.
With positive weights, Dijkstra processes vertices after all shorter predecessors are finalized.
For an equal-distance relaxation, add path counts and update min/max edge counts too.
analogy: Along with the cheapest arrival, keep how many equally cheap routes arrived and their fewest and most flights.
example: If two shortest routes to a city have four and six edges, the count includes both and the edge range is [4,6].
algorithm: Run Dijkstra while maintaining dist, ways, minEdges, maxEdges. A strictly shorter route replaces all four values; an equal route adds ways modulo 1e9+7 and combines edge extrema.
correctness: Positive edge lengths ensure a shortest predecessor is processed before its destination; every shortest route is then counted through its final edge, with extrema combined over all ties.
complexity: O((n+m) log n) time and O(n+m) space.
